body:
The Tower of Gael is the explorers’ protected home in Gael, a refuge associated with Nuru’s Eye in a land devastated by Death. Its courts, rooms and kitchen give adventurers somewhere to recover; its later history brings researchers, displaced families and the work of building permanent homes.

Home of the explorers and Nuru's Eye. Bane to all undead and fiends. A refuge in a hard and unforgiving land.The Tower’s founding description

Nuru’s Eye and the sentinel boundary

The Tower’s statues mark a practical boundary between relative safety and the dangerous land beyond. Residents speak of going beyond the statues as leaving protection. Gartina chooses ground within the sentinels for her first growing experiments; returning adventurers hurry into the safety of the courts.

Nuru’s Eye belongs to the sanctuary’s sacred and defensive identity. The Tower’s beacon and lighthouse imagery evoke its watch, but the Eye’s full nature, protective range and relationship to every sentinel remain uncertain. The Tower’s description as a bane to undead and fiends does not establish unlimited protection throughout Gael.

Rooms, kitchen, forge and roof

The Tower is a lived-in home, with personal quarters, hallways, a kitchen, work areas and a forge, roof access and an altar. Huoth’s welcome also describes a library, arcanum and meditation chambers. A complete floor plan and the building’s original construction remain unknown.

Gartina cooks, bakes and shares food in the kitchen. People return exhausted, retire to their rooms, meet in the halls and welcome newcomers. When Krone asks where to find the kitchen, Scribonia directs him higher in the Tower. Ordinary routines persist between dangerous expeditions.

The roof later serves a defensive purpose: Erebus moves supplies down to refugees without opening the doors in a dangerous situation. Shelter and aid must sometimes be arranged together with careful control of access.

Huoth and the altar of Nuru

Huoth is the early caretaker and intermediary through whom the explorers seek Nuru’s guidance. Residents report discoveries and threats to him. His watch is bound to the sanctuary; the adventurers must carry the work beyond its boundary.

At the altar, offerings—especially husks—accompany petitions for items, rare materials and help. After Nienna’s death, Saray and Elenia consider Huoth, Nuru and the altar as possible sources of resurrection assistance. Later arrivals learn the familiar practice of gathering husks in the Plains and requesting what they need.

Huoth’s physical watch ends on 3 March 2025 after the adventurers defeat the final major force threatening the restored lands. His later identification as an angel of Nuru comes through a shadow or echo at the altar. That encounter does not establish that he has resumed living in the Tower.

Missing Prima, committing to Gael

Early residents are far from home. Saray misses Pristinia; Gartina shares the feeling. Contact with Scribonia in Prima is limited by the cost and twenty-five-word constraint of Sending. They can sometimes communicate without being able to return casually.

We seem to be kind of stuck in a situation where the only way out is through.Gartina

The responsibilities outside the Tower give staying a purpose. Saray’s interest in restoring Gael grows alongside her longing for Prima. The refuge becomes home through repeated work, friendship and the difficulty of leaving that work unfinished.

Gartina and Saray’s restoration work

Beyond the sentinels, sour gas, damaged soil and failed plant growth make survival an environmental problem as well as a military one. Gartina proposes starting cultivation within the protected border and moving outward if it succeeds.

She identifies sulfur as a likely contributor to acidic soil and considers limestone, calcium and magnesium as remedies. This is her working explanation, rather than a complete diagnosis of every force damaging Gael. Saray suggests shellfish and crustacean shells as a local source of calcium.

Can you imagine we can fix this. And bring life and prosperity back here.Saray

By December 2024, obtaining substantial limestone and transporting it from Prima has become a practical supply problem. Restoration demands materials and journeys as well as a promising idea.

Dale’s return and another friend to recover

The Tower scene posted on 9 July records Dale awakening after Elenia’s diamond-assisted prayer. Saray embraces him, then tells him Nienna has died. Recovering one friend leaves another urgent need: Elenia no longer has a diamond large enough for Nienna’s return.

Dale joins the effort to obtain it, gives his husks and proposes larger hunting parties. The Tower is a place where recovery leads back into responsibility, rather than making the earlier deaths disappear.

Nienna · grief, resources and Raise Dead

Saray brings Nienna’s body home after their fatal encounter with soul eaters and wraiths on the Plains of Trial. The Tower becomes a place of grief and urgent planning. Saray blames herself; Elenia mourns; companions discuss diamonds, offerings and divine assistance. Their distress does not make Saray’s guilt proof of responsibility.

The 15 July scene supplies the outcome that those plans alone could not establish. Saray petitions Nuru’s messenger, offers husks and gold, and obtains a diamond at the altar. She gives it to Elenia, whose Raise Dead restores Nienna. Nienna wakes in alarm before being reassured that she is safe. This return precedes the September Hallowing sacrifice.

5 August 2024 · Moirah and Jiangshi

Moirah’s return with Jiangshi reaches the Tower at personal cost. The landmark becomes a place of resurrection and aftermath, where bringing someone home matters as much as setting out. The exact mechanism and full price remain part of their individual histories.

Warping lattice, Life and the Golden Tree

Scribonia studies contamination, warping lattice crystals and the reach of cleansing magic. Comparisons with the Etz Chaim branch and Life-associated energy raise a difficult possibility: Life and Death may not be simple opposites at the level of raw magical power. His comparisons and experiments remain research, rather than a settled universal explanation.

Adelia and Gartina’s efforts contribute to the Golden Tree. Residents later believe it helps clear Gael’s gloom. The achievement supports their hope that the land can recover, without proving that the Tree alone causes every improvement.

Hope and Adelia’s history extend beyond the Tower. The refuge is where people discuss those developments, plan experiments and bring their understanding back to the community; it is not the site of every event they describe.

A campaign that needs more than one safe base

Wrath shapes the expedition’s strategy. People scout, compare threats and discuss how to reach positions far from the Tower. In September 2024, Scribonia considers another tower nearer Wrath’s stronghold, with a broken teleportation circle that might be repaired for a forward base.

Circle travel offers the prospect of supplies, reinforcement and evacuation. Scribonia explains rune sequences as magical keys to doors. Developing transport changes the isolated expedition into a network of safer positions, without making every distant tower or circle part of this building.

Shipwreck survivors and the settlement outside

By early 2025, displaced people shelter near the Tower. Refugees whose ship crashed near Crustacean Cove live in huts, shacks and occasional magical shelter. Dale offers construction help and proposes reusing wreckage for homes.

On 24 February, Gartina and Dale begin with soup and conversation, then consider a salvaged longhouse and safer sources of material in the Plains. Their plan includes asking the refugees what they want. Permanent housing is a community decision as well as a building task.

A later refugee camp is devastated and survivors are recovered. Erebus checks on those brought back to the Tower. The crisis renews its oldest obligation: providing refuge when people lose the places where they were trying to live.

Rebuilding and civic responsibility

In 2026, discussions turn to permanent homes, fishing, boats, food production, smithing and settlement leadership. Erebus develops a mediating role between Tower staff, refugees and adventurers. That work reflects a community whose needs now extend beyond organizing the next expedition.

By September 2026, Lucido Spettoro reports three completed refugee homes and says the number is nowhere near enough. Building has begun, but emergency shelter and unfinished infrastructure remain part of life around the Tower.

The Tower is a civic anchor. Its importance does not establish it as Gael’s formal political capital, nor prove that a settlement was its builders’ original intention.

The watch inherited

Who built the Tower, what exactly is Nuru’s Eye, and how do its protections work? What lasting laws and institutions will grow around it? Those questions remain open, alongside the eventual scale and security of the civilian settlements.

The Tower’s known history is already larger than its walls: a protected home that gives people enough safety to study the land, mourn their companions and help others build lives beyond the refuge.

The Sanctum, library and Crucible

The Sanctum of the Wise is described as the top room of the Tower: a place to rest and, if fortunate or in real need of counsel, commune with Nuru. That description establishes its use without promising every visitor an audience or providing a complete floor plan.

The Library of Nuru preserves spells and research used by residents trying to understand Gael. Saray’s later list of uninvestigated sites shows the limits of that knowledge: having a library does not mean the island’s past has already been solved.

At the Tower’s pinnacle, the Crucible turns sanctuary into preparation. Huoth credits Cala’s idea and Nuru’s magic while stressing cooperation. These named spaces extend the Tower’s known functions without assuming how every chamber fits together.

Fenwick’s Tower · refuge, study and isolation

Fenwick’s March 2025 guide describes a defensible refuge marked by a persistent light. He compares it to a lighthouse and wonders whether it could aid navigation through the Void. The light and refuge belong to his account; the proposed Void function remains speculation.

He describes the Library of Nuru as a substantial research collection with spells catalogued by adventurers, separate from Pristinia’s holdings. He reports long solitary study and scribing a seventh-level spell. His belief that Nuru intended a counterpart to Pristinia’s repository is his reading of divine purpose, not an independently established founding account.

In the Sanctum of the Wise he describes old art, scrolls and reading material alongside space for rest, planning and manuscript work. He interprets these contents as evidence of Nuru’s care for knowledge and history. Possible communion does not promise an audience. His longing for Herb’s sandwiches and the Common Man also preserves how distant home felt during that first exploration.

A room for knowledge and commitments

Inside the Tower, the Library of Nuru supplies a distinct history of copying spells, uncertain research, shared meals and preparation. The later welcome of Fenwick to the Veilguard takes place there. The collection has useful records and real gaps; the Tower’s shelter does not make every question answerable from its shelves.

Scene references: 1, 2, 3, 4.

Keeping Selwyn’s body while a branch remains

Ryvyt reports bringing Selwyn’s body back and placing it in a room in the Knights’ tower. This report should not be confused with identifying every Gael tower as one building. Later, at the Tower of Gael, Fenwick casts Gentle Repose after considering the remaining black branch.

The narrator confirms that the spell works but that the branch neither moves nor changes. The body receives care; Selwyn’s return to life, removal of the branch and a complete explanation of its effects remain unestablished.

A return brings questions to the library

The Tower receives incomplete news as well as exhausted travelers. After returning with Bitoshi, Adelia finds Nienna in the library, frustrated over research. She says seven companions stayed behind at the tomb and describes how little magic she had left. Nienna presses her for the enemy’s strength and what the company has found.

Adelia prepares spells while they consider who might help. Their exchange in the Library of Nuru establishes a place where research can become a warning and a proposed response. It does not, on its own, establish that a relief party reached the tomb or carried out the measures they discuss.

What should be built outside first?

The settlement around the Tower also becomes a place of disagreement. Lucido argues that refugee homes must come before the market taking shape outside. Farkur describes fishing, employment and trade as a way to fund a community, then offers materials for a house and paid building work. Both discuss shelter, but their proposed sequences differ.

Lucido proposes paying refugees to help build the homes they need. Later he reports three houses completed while stressing how much remains. Those reports support a history of work in progress; they do not settle every resident’s priorities or establish finished permanent housing. The Tower’s protection gives people a base for this argument and work, not an automatic answer to either.

The company gathers to petition the gods

Scribonia brings companions to the Tower and asks its visitors to help request a divine audience. Adelia comes when he calls, Elenia leaves her material work, and Arjahn joins the gathering. Nymera, Olokun, Oya and Alyhotep bring their own questions, prayers and ordinary care into the room.

The disagreement is substantial. Scribonia wants an independent account and accepts a representative or later reply. Elenia considers some questions answered already and worries about wasting the gods’ time. Arjahn needs to hear whether his fighting matters. Their petitions are made; the first follow-up leaves the tap on Arjahn’s shoulder and Adelia’s requested checks unexplained. A later continuation supplies individual replies.

The Tower’s altar is a place to ask, without guaranteeing an audience. Adelia also corrects the assumption that the Tower itself is her domain: she says her power is strongest near Hope. The setting remains distinct from the tree and every other sacred site.

Read the full gathering, disagreement, prayers and farewells →

Individual replies after the gathering

The continuation gives the Tower’s petitions a response without turning the gathering into a completed divine assembly. Adelia receives words individually and chooses to repeat only part, concerning wisdom and mistakes. After the gathering has dispersed, Heimr answers Arjahn instead of Talan. Their conversation ends with Arjahn’s question about grief and Heimr’s promise to get him to his family when it is over.

Neither exchange supplies every answer sought by the company, and the record does not make every companion a witness to Arjahn’s conversation. The promised reunion has not happened. Fenwick’s separate departure for Prima, with his homunculus and simulacrum, also confirms that the Tower remains a place people pass through rather than the destination of every ongoing expedition.
